title: Customer voices
say: In customer discovery, I heard: Finding a bond’s CUSIP is such a pain. I don’t know where to buy. Fidelity’s bond account is not for me. I only want to invest a small amount. Different comments, one design challenge: getting started.
screen: Show quote cards 01, 02, 03 and 04 in sequence. Keep each on screen for about six seconds. Quotes are edited for clarity; do not invent names, ages or interview counts.

title: The design question
say: How can someone with no bond experience understand a few options and make their first small purchase? That’s the question behind InCreditble.
screen: Show the welcome with Your first bond. At your pace. Enter Overview, point briefly to the sample connected account, then click Find a bond.

title: Start with the person
say: First, I tell the product I’m new to bonds. That changes how much explanation I get. My risk preference is separate. Then I choose a yield target, a timeframe, an industry and a budget. Let’s start with just twenty-five dollars.
screen: From a reset demo, complete Continue with a demo identity. Keep I’m new to bonds and Balanced. Click Choose my preferences. Keep 4.50%, up to 5 years and Any sector; change amount to $25. Click Find my bonds.

title: Replace the search burden
say: I don’t need to start with a bond identifier. The finder gives me three matches within my preferences. I can compare an earlier repayment date, a different industry and more interest, with the important trade-offs visible.
screen: Show Marketlane Stores · 1Y, Cedar Healthcare and Sunfield Foods · 2Y. Scroll slowly enough to read the comparison labels. Return to Marketlane and click Ask AI.

title: Explain before the decision
say: When I need help, I can ask about the company or what could go wrong. Here, the assistant explains the risk of missed payments and selling early. The explanations are optional; the decision stays with me.
screen: Choose What are the risks? Pause on the actual answer. Click Back to bond details. Point briefly to the company description. Click Choose an amount.

title: A small purchase with clear terms
say: Now I see a sample price, with separate buy and sell quotes. My twenty-five dollars buys part of a bond. Before confirming, I can see exactly what I pay, the cash I’ll have left, expected interest and the repayment date. These are promised payments, not guaranteed returns.
screen: Wait for the demo quote. Continue with this price. Keep $25 and click Review simulated order. Pause on Total you pay, Cash afterward and payment preview. Check the simulation acknowledgment and click Confirm simulated buy.

title: Close the loop
say: After I approve, the new holding appears and my cash balance updates. The payment view helps me see when interest is expected. Existing sample accounts stay visible alongside this position, so I can see the wider picture.
screen: Click See updated holdings. Show the new Marketlane position and cash change. Click Payments, select April, and point to the new expected interest entry. Avoid showing a second transaction.

title: What works underneath
say: Underneath, explicit filters and transparent ranking narrow a pool of 672 fictional bonds. The prototype tracks fractional positions, settlement, cost basis and payment schedules. Assistant responses, identity checks, quotes and connections are simulated; no live AI model or broker is connected.
screen: Hold on the product or use a simple caption: Filters → Explained matches → User confirmation → Updated holdings. Keep a clear prototype label; do not show invented architecture or provider logos.

title: Return to the user
say: Next, we’ll test whether first-time investors can explain their purchase and its risks without coaching. InCreditble. Your first bond. At your pace.
screen: Show closing card 05. End at 2:58 or earlier; no long outro. Do not add a claim of validated customer adoption.
